subject: Post-call recap: HelioAI trial — load signature & benchmark requests
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@helioai.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: HelioAI trial — load signature & benchmark requests

Hi Sara — great chat earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before we spin up the trial environment. TL;DR: we need a small sample of production traffic + a clear success criteria so we can design the POC runbook.

Call highlights:
- Primary goal: validate cost/latency profile for your real-time summarization endpoint and confirm a predictable path to production.
- Typical production pattern you mentioned: steady background traffic (~20 RPS) with periodic bursts up to ~180–220 RPS lasting ~20–60s during market-moving events.
- Typical request sizes: median 120 tokens (user prompt + system context), 75th ~300 tokens, occasional outliers ~1,200 tokens (batch / report-generation).
- Concurrency target: ~50 concurrent sessions (user-facing), with up to ~400 simultaneous short-lived async jobs during batch runs.

Requested artifacts from HelioAI:
1) A redacted traffic sample CSV (timestamp, route, avg_tokens, peak_tokens, response_ms) — attach small slice if possible.
2) A short prompt set for quality/regression checks (10–20 prompts).
3) Any hard SLOs you want enforced for the trial (e.g., 95th percentile p-gen latency <200ms for median prompts).

Proposed POC plan and success criteria (draft):
- Duration: 2 weeks (pilot run + readout). Start target: week of 2026-05-11.
- Baseline bench: run controlled synthetic replay to validate throughput and 95/99 latency curves.
- Production-ish replay: run sampled traffic at production concurrency for 4–6 hours to observe burst behavior and autoscaling.
- Success metrics: 95th latency under 200ms for median/short prompts; error rate <0.5%; token cost within target band (TBD with your finance).
- Ownership: Redwood engineer (Priyom) will own runtime provisioning and telemetry; Karthik will coordinate business/ops; Helio will provide traffic CSV and sample prompts.

Attachments: I’ve attached a small template CSV (traffic_sample.csv) and a draft POC SLA (redwood-poc-sla.pdf). Also linking a shared Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/helioai-poc-traffic

Next steps: can you confirm the traffic numbers above and upload a 1–2 day redacted sample (or paste a short snippet) so Priyom can finalize the config? Also confirm target start week.

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Sara Li <sara.li@helioai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@helioai.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: HelioAI trial — load signature & benchmark requests

Thanks for the clear recap, Karthik. All looks right directionally; a couple clarifications from our side: 

- The steady-state is closer to 18–25 RPS depending on the hour; bursts are spikey and can hit ~250 RPS for ~30–90s during major events (not every day).
- Median tokens ~110–130, 90th ~480 (we have a small percentage of long-form report requests that go to ~1,500 tokens).
- For concurrency: 50 interactive + ~350 async jobs is accurate. Async jobs tend to have higher token counts and we typically batch them in short bursts.

We can upload a 48-hour redacted sample to the Drive by EOD tomorrow. For the prompt set, we’ll provide 15 representative prompts (mix of short replies and long reports).

Timeline: week of 2026-05-11 works for us. One ask — we need to see the trial run results before we commit to any reserved capacity; can Redwood run the production-ish replay and provide a readout with token-cost estimates?

Also attaching a small log excerpt (pasted below) — we'll put the CSV in the Drive with the filename helio_48h_sample.csv.

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@helioai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: HelioAI trial — load signature & benchmark requests

Thanks Sara — that helps. A few technical clarifications so we size correctly and ensure the replay is faithful: 

1) Tokenization: do your server logs report tokens measured client-side or after our tokenizer? If client-side, please indicate tokenizer used (we can re-tokenize during replay).
2) Session affinity: are interactive sessions sticky to a user session for >30s (i.e., reuse KV cache) or are most requests independent? This will change cache hit assumptions.
3) Async job batching: are those jobs sent as single requests with large token counts, or does your pipeline send multiple parallel smaller requests that you aggregate later?
4) Any per-request weight or priority rules (e.g., premium users get priority routing) we should model during the replay?

Technical plan: we’ll do two phases — (A) controlled microbench (synthetic short/long prompts) to establish baseline latency curves across instance types, and (B) production-ish replay using your CSV mapped to our route configs (we’ll preserve timestamps to reproduce bursts). For phase B we’ll run at your stated concurrency for a 4–6 hour window to capture autoscale behavior.

Can you drop the CSV to the Drive and grant redwood-poc@redwood.com read access? Also, if you have sample system prompts (the instructions that sit at the top of every request), please include them so we can evaluate quality/regression.

I’ll own the runtime side and will post a bench plan by EOD today.

— Priyom
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@helioai.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: HelioAI trial — load signature & benchmark requests

Perfect — thanks for the fast responses. Finalizing owners and immediate next steps: 

- Owners: Priyom (runtime & bench), Monica (customer success / onboarding), Karthik (deal / commercial).
- Actions for HelioAI: upload helio_48h_sample.csv to the Drive and grant redwood-poc@redwood.com read access; drop the prompt set in the same folder (15 prompts); confirm any compliance controls (they flagged SOC2 earlier).
- Actions for Redwood: Priyom to provision a trial cluster (standard-medium) with autoscale enabled and run phase A microbench on Mon 2026-05-11; Phase B replay scheduled Tue 2026-05-12 09:00–15:00 PT (4–6 hours) — we’ll share a runbook beforehand.
- Success criteria (finalize after we see sample): target 95th latency <200ms for median prompts, acceptable token cost estimate (we’ll include a per-token estimate in readout), and functional parity on the 15 prompt test set (no more than 2% quality regressions vs your baseline).

If that all sounds good I’ll send a calendar invite for the bench kickoff and a short runbook link (HubSpot deal link: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deal/DL-2026-1389). Also attaching the draft POC SLA for review (redwood-poc-sla.pdf).

Best — Karthik

--
